title: Brothers' and sister's talents; mother and the Hammond organ
summary: His second brother was a gifted violinist who gave it up for football, his sister graduated in music, and his mother could play Bach but not improvise.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, but my second brother was really the most -- probably the greatest talent, he was a great violinist. He had a lot of scholarships offered him and he won a lot of things, but --
Really?
-- he was also a football player.
For heaven's sake.
And it kind of broke my father's heart and said that's for sissies, not for football players and he wouldn't play anymore.
Oh, what a shame, eh?
My sister was always -- played piano and everything. She -- she graduated in music. She was a college-aholic, I think. She just kept always going to college.
Oh, really?
Oh, yeah. And she taught school --
Did she teach music, you mean?
Well, she taught regular school, then she she played organ --
Oh.
All these things, so --
Well that was --

-- it's strange cause my mother would always say, she couldn't improvise a note, but she could play anything, all these powerful Bach things --, when I'd go home I'd ask her -- we'd go over to the church and she'd play on that organ, and she had a Hammond organ at the house. So my mother used to laugh said if she could play at the skating rink and play jazz, like you do, she'd be the happiest person in the world.
Oh, isn't that funny, she minded that
she couldn't improvise.
Yeah, she knew so much music, and knew all about it, and yet she couldn't -- she used to say how do you do it, I'd say, I don't know, Portia, I really don't know.
Isn't that something. And of course --
Yeah?
-- the -- the violin ist -- I suppose something that -- with violin music I -- I mean would he improvise or did he even --
No, I don't remember that, I was rather young when he played --
Yeah, yeah.
-- then he went off --I know I was quite young when he went off to college.
Yeah, yeah.
And --
Yeah.
